entries.text: notebook: updated Gorrak Vael

You spit the gag clear and drive your forehead at the grey cloak's helm. It glances off the iron rim and stings more than it hurts. Then you roar through the shutters at Dreg to break the stair door, take the gate-top and not let them hang Gorrak. Behind you, Tessa's hand is already at her hair.

Her hairpin is in the wall-ring's lock before the next breath, and it clicks open. Her wrist is free.

You do not see the sword. The grey cloak you butted was waiting for a gap in your guard, and the edge comes down across your chest as a red crack of pain. It takes the last hit point you were holding. The room goes grey at the edges, then dark. The last thing you hear is the Foreman's soft voice saying, "Alive. I want him alive."

The last thing you feel is a small, cold, quick hand at your throat, and Tessa's voice, rough with fear, saying your name.

You come back slowly. You hear it first: boots on stone, a Tally voice shouting orders in Goblin, and somewhere beyond the wall a low rhythmic thumping, spear butts on slate. Someone has laid a cloak over you. It is a little before nine in the morning, and you have 1 hit point. The wire and the cuffs are gone from your wrists, cut off with a chisel and a mallet, and the skin beneath is raw to the meat.

You are in the ledger-house, on the floor by the stove. The shutters are open on a hard white winter sky. Tessa kneels beside you with her left arm in a sling, and her face is bruised and pale and fierce. "Alive," she says. "You always are, you stubborn goat." Her hand finds yours. Her fingers are shaking.

She tells it fast. Dreg and the Tallies broke the stair door in the second round. The grey cloaks fought on the walk and in the doorway, but there were twenty spears in the yard, and the Foreman's men had sixty paces of stone to hold. They didn't hold it. Dreg cut Gorrak and Krell down from the beam himself, before the bell had finished. Gorrak is alive, with new stitches and a hoarse voice, and the Tallies are calling him captain again.

"The Foreman's gone," Tessa says. "The bedchamber door was open when they got to it. The chest is gone, and the ledger with it. There's a stair behind the wall, an old shaft-stair, the kind that goes down into the workings, and there's blood on the steps. Not much." She takes a breath. "He's wounded, Kor, and he's got the book and the key chain, and nobody has found him."

Across the room Gorrak stands in the doorway, a long grey shape against the sky, bareheaded with the burn on his face. Dreg is a pace behind him. They are looking at you.

You are at 1 hit point, free of iron, and the morning is cold and clear. What does Korvash do?

The axe slips from your fingers, and every eye on the shelf follows it down. It never reaches the ground. Your boot-toe catches the haft, flicks it up into both hands, and you are already running, roaring, with the rage hot behind your teeth.

You close the gap before Skarn finishes drawing breath. Your blow comes round in a hard arc at his knife arm, but he is quicker than he looks. He jerks back, the edge hisses past his chest, and the knife leaves the young Tally's throat. Not by your doing, but by his own flinch. The bound man staggers, falls and rolls clear of the cairn's foot. Skarn drops him without a glance.

Then the bows speak. Two of the six sing at once: one bolt skates off your scales and the other bites into your shoulder, but the rage turns most of the sting aside. Skarn swings a blade at you as you stand over him, and it opens a shallow line across your ribs. You are at 15 of 23 hit points. The other four crossbows have sagged, their men not sure they want to be here. They watch, and have not yet fired.

It is your turn again, with Skarn within reach, the two archers who shot you a few paces to his left, the four who wavered beyond them, and the bound Tally lying near your feet. You are raging, with one rage and your breath weapon still in hand. Your Reckless Attack leaves their attacks with advantage until your next turn.

When he was young, hobgoblins of the Iron Tallies warband, led by a tin-masked captain named Gorrak Vael (who notches a rod for every raid), overran his village. His father Dargan held the narrow Goat's Throat pass, losing a hand and then his life, so the herd and the children could flee; Korvash swore to him, with his blood on his hands, to protect the weak. His younger sister Tessa was lost in the raid and her fate is UNKNOWN: he never saw her fall and has never stopped wondering, so she must not be confirmed alive or dead unless discovered in play. The survivors fled to Harrowmere, where his aunt Veshra raised him and still sends word by travelers. The clan built a cairn at the Goat's Throat, which he has never had the heart to revisit. line:
I raise my fist to the slab crews and keep it raised, whispering to Gorrak, "Hold until the file is strung out on the narrow, and not before." I tell Dreg to send two spears to meet the four heading for the Weeping Ledge, quietly, since they'll find it empty and then try to flank us.

When the first torch reaches the tight bend, I drop my fist and roar, "Slabs, now! Slingers, loose!", then step into the road with shield up beside Gorrak to hold the head of the column.

character.name: Grunna Holt
character.personality: Blunt, stubborn and loyal to the bone. Hard on her kin, harder on herself. Keeps her word and expects others to keep theirs.
character.appearance: Broad, grey-green half-orc woman with a weathered caravan guard's face, short-cropped dark hair and a notched left tusk.

entries.text: Before I resolve this charge, I have to correct something I told you earlier. I said I had no way to build a new character. That was wrong: I have a `new_pc` tool for exactly this. Because of that mistake, Grunna has been running without a real sheet. I'll build it properly now.

I'm stopping before the ambush springs, because I owe you a correction. Earlier I told you I couldn't build Grunna's sheet. That was wrong. A tool for making a new character after a death exists, and I should have used it. Until now she has been running on my notes, with no tracked HP or gear. Since a fight is about to start, I'm fixing that first.

Here is her real sheet, built from your choices:

Grunna Holt, half-orc fighter 1, acolyte. HP 12, AC 18 (chain mail and shield), speed 30, proficiency +2, passive Perception 13, darkvision 60 ft.
STR 17 (+3), DEX 13 (+1), CON 15 (+2), INT 8 (-1), WIS 12 (+1), CHA 10 (+0).
Saves: STR +5 and CON +4. Skills: Athletics +5, Perception +3, Insight +3, Intimidation +2, Religion +1.
Longsword +5 to hit, 1d8+3 (1d10+3 two-handed). Light crossbow +3 to hit, 1d8+1, with 20 bolts.
Second Wind (heal 1d10+1 as a bonus action, once per rest). Relentless Endurance (drop to 1 HP instead of 0, once per long rest). Savage Attacks (extra weapon die on a melee crit). Protection (reaction: impose disadvantage on an attack against an ally next to you while you hold a shield).
Gear: explorer's pack, 15 gp, amulet, prayer wheel, vestments, incense.

Two details are mine, because you didn't specify them. She speaks Goblin and Draconic as her two background languages, and her alignment is Lawful Good. Say so if you'd rather change either.

Two earlier rolls were also wrong. Her chain mail gives disadvantage on Stealth, which I did apply. But her Intimidation and Perception were right at +2 and +3, and I treated her as having no Second Wind or Relentless Endurance. Those both count now.

Do you say yes to this sheet? If so, I'll confirm it. Then I'll start the fight at the switchback with your orders, and with Grunna at 12 HP and AC 18.
